_: Marquee design tokens — the single source of truth. Edit, then run: python3 tools/build-tokens.py
_lineage: Carried over from playnite_clean/design/tokens.json. The palette and the shape values are identical, because the design is the same one and it was already approved.
_freedom: Several tokens in the Playnite version existed only to work around WPF: no letter-spacing, no saturation filter, no clamped radii, a fixed 1080px canvas. All of that is now possible. It is permission, not instruction — the design as tuned is the approved one.

palette._: One black, one white, one focus grey. Every surface is pure black: panels, sections, page. Separation comes from the hairline and from the focus grey, never from a second black. Written #AARRGGBB to stay diffable against the sibling projects; the build converts to rgba().

_decisions.accent: Near-white, not gold. A saturated accent competes with cover art on every screen and dates quickly; white selection is what PS5 and the Apple TV interface both do.
_decisions.focus: Ring plus a small lift. In the Playnite build the scale had to stay at 1 because growing a card changed how the list measured itself and shifted column counts mid-navigation. Here the grid positions cards with its own transform and does its arithmetic on the unscaled box, so an inner element can scale freely and reflow nothing. Set to 1 to turn it off.
_decisions.ring: --ring-offset must equal --ring-w. The ring is drawn outset by the offset with that thickness; if they differ, a hairline gap opens between ring and card. This cost an afternoon in the Playnite build.
_decisions.coverRatio: 2:3, the real box-art ratio. Playnite's grid forced 3:4 and could not be told otherwise. We are not Playnite.
_decisions.gapX: Horizontal gutters are wider than vertical ones, 42 against 30. Cards are portrait, so equal gaps read as tighter side to side -- the eye measures a gap against the edge it runs along, and a 2:3 card has a long vertical edge and a short horizontal one. The vertical gap also has to be larger than --card-shadow-reach: scrolling up spends the difference clearing the shadow of the row above, and whatever is left is the space above the focused row.
_decisions.scroll: Moving between rows glides rather than jumps, over --scroll-ms. Eased out rather than in-out: a button press is an instruction, and easing into it reads as lag. The glide retargets rather than restarting, because the repeat rate (95ms) is faster than the glide, so a held direction would otherwise stutter at exactly the moment smoothness matters. Set to 0 for instant, which is also what prefers-reduced-motion gives.
_decisions.shadowReach: How far a card's shadow reaches past its own box, and the amount the grid scrolls *past* a row's gap so the previous row's shadow lands exactly on the top edge. Without it, scrolling up leaves a smudge and a sliver of the card above. Keep it in step with the box-shadow in app.css -- its Y offset plus its blur. The shadow was tightened from 10/24 to 5/14 for this: the clearance it costs comes out of the space above the focused row, so a softer shadow buys a roomier grid.
